clue.text: Sleeping bag may cause amusement

definitions.meaning: a roll of bedding a camper sleeps in
split as ..., to be funny enough to make people laugh

explanation.surface: A sleeping bag that turns out to be funny.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition only works if the answer is split into two words, BE DROLL: to be comic, which may amuse people.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolled-up bundle of bedding serves as a camper's sleeping bag; read as two words it means to act comically.

clue.text: Daphne, for example, has one answer to a code of morals!

parts.note: daphne is a kind of flowering shrub
I is the Roman numeral one
to answer can mean to serve or suffice, as in that will do

explanation.surface: A woman named Daphne holds the key to a moral code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daphne' looks like a woman's name, but it is a shrub. 'answer' means suffice: DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushido is the Japanese samurai code of honour and conduct.

clue.text: It beats a portion of chicken

definitions.meaning: a stick used by a percussion player
the lower leg of a cooked fowl

explanation.surface: Something that beats a helping of chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: A drummer strikes with sticks of this name; the lower leg of a cooked bird has the same name.

clue.text: Manually operated vehicle?

parts.note: manuals are keyboards played by hand, and a vehicle is a means of expressing something, as a newspaper is

explanation.surface: A car you drive by hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vehicle' suggests a car; here it means a means of expression, such as a party newspaper, and 'manually' points to the keyboards of a church instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The church instrument is played on manuals, and the word also means a mouthpiece or publication.

clue.text: Distinctive feature in the East forming part of a dirge

indicators.note: forming part of means the first pieces are placed within the word for a dirge

parts.note: a lament is a song of mourning, a dirge
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: An eastern feature in a funeral song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forming part of' puts IN and E inside LAMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A lineament is a characteristic line or feature, usually of the face.

clue.text: Outstanding writing, one may feel

parts.note: outstanding is read literally as standing out from the page: raised dots that blind readers touch

explanation.surface: Praise for superb prose that moves the reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' seems to mean excellent, but it means raised up from the paper, and 'feel' means touch with the fingertips.
explanation.definitionFit: The tactile script for blind readers is made of raised dots felt with the fingers.

clue.text: It's marshy ground that's supporting the coach

parts.note: a bog is marshy ground
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Marshy ground under a coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' is a railway carriage, not a trainer or bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A bogie is the wheeled undercarriage on which a railway carriage rests.

clue.text: Let out into the field, free to move about

indicators.note: into means the shuffled letters are put inside the word for field

parts.note: arable describes ploughed field land

indicators.note: out means the word Let is put out of order

explanation.surface: A horse let out into the field, free to roam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LET into LTE; 'into' puts it inside ARABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open to change is not fixed in place.

clue.text: It's working everybody up in Venezuela, that's plain

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters read from the bottom upward, that is backwards

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is on
all means everybody

explanation.surface: Everyone at work in Venezuela, clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ON and ALL together backwards. 'in Venezuela, that's' narrows the definition: the word is South American.
explanation.definitionFit: The llanos are the grassy plains of Venezuela and Colombia.

clue.text: Said I lived hard? Rubbish!

indicators.note: said means the letter I is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like EYE
was means lived or existed
H stands for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone claiming a tough life, and a listener calling it rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' makes I into EYE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is nonsense or humbug.

clue.text: To knock out middleweights was painful

parts.note: to knock someone out is to stun them

indicators.note: middle asks for the central letter of the word weights, which has seven letters

explanation.surface: A boxer was hurt by being knocked out at middleweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middleweights' looks like a boxing class, but it splits into 'middle' and 'weights': G is the middle letter of WEIGHTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that stung hurt sharply, as a smack or a nettle does.

clue.text: Get cash for treat

definitions.meaning: to convert a cheque or bill into money
to treat with someone is to bargain or hold talks

explanation.surface: Cashing in to pay for a treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank negotiates a cheque when it turns it into money; to treat with an enemy is to bargain for terms.

clue.text: Suggest disposing of annuities

indicators.note: disposing of something can mean arranging it, so these letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: Advice to sell off one's annuities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposing of' looks like selling, but it means arranging: the letters of ANNUITIES are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To insinuate is to hint at something indirectly rather than say it outright.

clue.text: Business on short time rejected this girl

indicators.note: rejected means the pieces are turned back, so the combined letters run backwards

parts.note: ado means fuss or business, as in much ado
HR is the short form of hour, a span of time

explanation.surface: A girl turned away because her firm is on short time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns ADO and HR together back to front, giving RH + ODA.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so it stands for a particular girl.

clue.text: Maintain view of wood with nothing in front

indicators.note: in front means the zero piece is placed before the timber piece

parts.note: O is the figure zero, nothing
pine is a kind of wood

explanation.surface: Someone keeping a view of woodland with nothing blocking it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maintain view' together is the definition: to maintain a view is to hold an opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to hold or state an opinion.

clue.text: Taxes discontinued lawsuits

parts.note: ex means former, no longer continuing
actions are lawsuits

explanation.surface: Taxes that ended lawsuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taxes' is a noun here, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactions are demands for payment, such as levies or tolls.

clue.text: Found form

definitions.meaning: to found an institution is to set it up
to form something is to create or set it up

explanation.surface: A form that has been found.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean to set up or create, as when founding a company or forming a club.

clue.text: Sadist of a climbing instructor?

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, something one goes climbing on
a mentor is an instructor or guide

explanation.surface: A cruel mountaineering instructor.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, the answer is the mentor of a tor, a teacher of hill climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentor is someone who inflicts suffering, as a sadist does.

clue.text: Barham's legendary creation — poor dying slob

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters of dying slob are in a sorry state, so rearranged

explanation.surface: An author's legendary character, a poor lazy man dying.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Barham wrote The Ingoldsby Legends under the pen name Thomas Ingoldsby, hence 'legendary'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Ingoldsby was the invented author of Barham's comic collection of legends.

clue.text: Resemble Kate, changing later

indicators.note: changing tells us the name Kate is altered into a new order

parts.note: after means later, as in soon after

explanation.surface: Kate looks like someone, and will change later on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges KATE into TAKE; 'later' supplies AFTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To take after a parent is to resemble them.

clue.text: Current state: has a hat on

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the hat word sits above the state

parts.note: a topi is a sun helmet
Cal is short for California

explanation.surface: Describing the current state of affairs: someone wearing a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: A TOPI is a pith helmet; CAL is a short form of California.
explanation.definitionFit: Topical means of current interest.

clue.text: It blights ears' growth — only pick odd ones

indicators.note: only pick odd ones means take the first, third, fifth letters and so on of the words ears' growth

explanation.surface: Something that blights growing ears of corn, and advice to pick only odd specimens.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of EARS GROWTH are E, R, G, O, T.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergot is a fungus that blights rye and other cereals.

clue.text: Your old source of DNA constituent

parts.note: thy is the old form of your
a mine is a source, as of information

explanation.surface: An old source of DNA material.
explanation.definitionFit: Thymine is one of the four bases in DNA.

clue.text: Spot Italian singer

parts.note: a pip is a spot, as on a dice or playing card
It is short for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: Picking out an Italian opera singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singer' is a songbird, not an opera star.
explanation.definitionFit: The pipit is a small songbird, and crosswords often call birds singers.

clue.text: Pain, touching a knife

indicators.note: touching means the two pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: a pang is a sharp pain

explanation.surface: A pain caused by touching a knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A panga is a broad African machete.

clue.text: With delight, find touch returning in close-catching position

indicators.note: in means the backwards touch word goes inside the cricket fielding position

parts.note: gully is a cricket fielding position close to the batsman, for taking catches

indicators.note: returning means the word for touch is read backwards

parts.note: to feel is to touch

explanation.surface: A cricketer happily finding the ball comes back to him near the bat.
explanation.walkthrough: GULLY is a fielding position in cricket, near the batsman on the off side. 'returning' turns FEEL into LEEF, which goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something with delight is to do it joyfully.

clue.text: Natural character in sound serial

definitions.meaning: the texture of wood or stone, or one's nature
a word that sounds like serial, cereal, is a kind of seed crop

explanation.surface: A natural character in a radio serial.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is spoken: 'serial' sounds like cereal, and wheat or barley is a cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: The texture of wood is its natural character; a cereal crop is seed such as wheat.

clue.text: Small line-up arouses passion

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for small line is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a serif is a small stroke at the end of a printed letter

explanation.surface: A short line-up stirs passions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line-up' looks like a queue, but splits: 'Small line' is SERIF, 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that fires you inflames or excites you.

clue.text: Eg, C for chiming

definitions.meaning: C is an example of a letter that is not a vowel
chiming in means agreeing, or sounding in harmony

explanation.surface: An example: C stands for chiming.
explanation.walkthrough: C looks like a musical note that might chime, but it is just a letter of the alphabet, and not a vowel.
explanation.definitionFit: C is a non-vowel letter; to be in harmony or agreement is the old sense of chiming together.

clue.text: Indian sage rejected title, having originally taken one

indicators.note: rejected means the title word is turned back to front

parts.note: Sir is a title given to a knight

indicators.note: originally asks for the first letter of having

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An Indian holy man who turned down a knighthood once he had accepted one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns SIR into RIS; 'originally' takes H from 'having'; 'taken' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A rishi is a Hindu seer or poet of the Vedic tradition.

clue.text: The sort of officer to find himself in the soup

definitions.meaning: an officer who keeps contact between units or groups

definitions.text: to find himself in the soup
definitions.meaning: in cooking, a thickening of egg yolk and cream for a soup or sauce

explanation.surface: The kind of officer who ends up in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the soup' looks like the idiom for trouble, but it is literal: the culinary term for a soup thickener.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison officer links groups; in cookery the word names a thickener of yolks and cream.

clue.text: Others see about new presentation

parts.note: the rest means the others

indicators.note: about means the cathedral see word is turned round

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Other people take a look at a new way of presenting something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is a bishop's see, not the verb: Ely, which 'about' turns round to YLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A restyle is a fresh design or new look for something.
